Behavioral fix on branch `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`, approved by Marcel after cross-checking the Jira AC, live Figma (Default vs Hover instances), and the current code.

**The confirmed bug:** the desktop prev/next arrows (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `carousel`/`arrowButton` parts) are currently gated only on `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` (`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — a *device-capability* check), so on any desktop/mouse device they are visible **permanently**, not just while the user is actually hovering the card. Per the AC ("when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear") and live Figma (the Carousel element is `hidden="true"` in every Default-state instance checked and only visible in the corresponding Hover-state instance, for both PLP and Wishlist), they should only appear during an actual hover/focus-within interaction — exactly like this same card's price/size-chip/notify-me reveals already work. The remove ('x') button is explicitly NOT part of this fix — confirmed correct as always-visible, leave it untouched.

**Read both files in full first**, they're not long:
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`

**The exact pattern to match** — this file already implements this correctly for `price`/`sizeChips`/`notifyMe`, inside `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s `root` part, nested inside its `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` block (search for `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` to find it):
```ts
[`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
  display: 'block',
},
[`&:focus-within [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.sizeChips}"]`]: {
  display: 'block',
},
```
`&` refers to the card's own root (this rule lives in the organism's `root` part), so hovering or focusing *anywhere* on the card — not just the image — triggers the reveal. That's deliberate (see the file's own Fix 2 comment above that block) and should apply to the arrows too, for the same reason: hovering the card's content area should reveal the arrows exactly the same as hovering the image does, matching the AC's "when the user hovers" (the whole card), not "when the user hovers the image specifically."

**Step 1 — `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`:** the `carousel` part currently has:
```ts
display: 'none',
...
[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
  display: 'flex',
},
```
Remove the `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: { display: 'flex' }` sub-block entirely — `carousel` should stay `display: 'none'` unconditionally at the Media-recipe level; the reveal now lives entirely in the organism's recipe (Step 2). Leave everything else in `carousel`/`arrowButton` (position, transform, paddingInline, pointerEvents, etc.) untouched.

**Step 2 — `zimmProductCard.css.ts`:** add a new, **unconditional** hover/focus-within reveal for the carousel inside the existing `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` block in the `root` part — unconditional because, unlike `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`/`hoverHidesPrice`/etc., the arrows apply the same way across every variation (home/plp/wishlist) whenever a card has more than one image; there is no `VARIATION_CONFIG` flag gating them today and this fix shouldn't invent one. Add:
```ts
[`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
  display: 'flex',
},
[`&:focus-within [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
  display: 'flex',
},
```
Place it sensibly among the other reveals in that block (read the surrounding comments first — match this file's own convention of a short comment above each block explaining what it does and citing evidence, the same way `hoverRevealsPrice`/`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector`/`hoverRevealsNotifyMe` each do). Note `carousel`'s own z-index fix already exists elsewhere in this same `root` part (unconditional, outside the media query) — don't duplicate or disturb that, this is a separate, additive rule.

**Before finishing, check one more thing yourself:** `ZimmProductCardMedia` has its own standalone Storybook stories (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.stories.tsx`, e.g. a `MultipleImages` story) that render it *without* the organism wrapping it. After this fix, Media's own `carousel` part has no self-contained reveal at all — only the organism's root `:hover`/`:focus-within` triggers it, so Media's standalone story can never show the arrows via CSS alone (there's no organism root to hover in that story). Check whether that story's existing doc comment already describes this as a "manual visual check only" limitation the same way this codebase already handles other hover-only behaviors it can't demonstrate via Storybook interaction tests (jsdom can't trigger real `:hover` regardless) — if the comment currently implies the story itself shows working hover-to-reveal arrows, correct it to state plainly that arrows are demonstrated at the organism level (`Commerce/ZimmProductCard`), not here, since this component alone no longer has anything that reveals them. Do not invent a new self-contained hover rule for Media just to preserve the old story behavior — that would reintroduce the exact bug being fixed (an image-only hover trigger instead of whole-card).

**Do not touch** anything related to `close`/the remove button — confirmed correct, out of scope for this fix. Do not touch any `VARIATION_CONFIG` flag or add a new one.

When done, report the exact before/after for both files and the story-comment check, confirm `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean, and run the full test suite (`npm run test`) to check for regressions — several existing tests likely assert on the *current* (buggy) carousel visibility behavior (e.g. asserting arrows are visible outside of a hover/focus-within simulation) and may need updating to match the corrected behavior; if so, update them to assert the new correct behavior (hidden by default, revealed under `:hover`/`:focus-within` on the card root) rather than weakening or deleting the assertions. Do not stage, do not commit.

2	import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';

7	 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
8	 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
9	 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
10	 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
11	 */
12	
13	/**
14	 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
15	 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Same `breakpoints` token and mobile-

17	 * uses, imported from the same place, so the two files can't drift on what "desktop" means here.
18	 */

20	
21	type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
22	  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer

25	  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override

28	  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
29	   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
30	   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
31	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
32	  /** Fix C — true whenever ZimmProductCardContent actually mounted a notify-me button
33	   *  (`isUnavailable && onNotifyMe`, computed once in index.tsx as `showNotifyMe`). Unlike the two
34	   *  flags above, the "hidden by default" half lives INSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, not outside it
35	   *  — see docblock point 4: a touch pointer must see notify-me unconditionally (confirmed via
36	   *  every Mobile Unavailable Figma reference), where price/the size-selector do the opposite. */
37	  hoverRevealsNotifyMe?: boolean;
38	  /** Fix C — true for a PLP/Wishlist card that would normally hover-swap to the size-selector
39	   *  (`config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector`) but is out of stock. Unlike every other flag here, this
40	   *  is not a pointer-type concern at all: the size-chip wrapper stays hidden permanently, in
41	   *  every state, on every device — see docblock point 4. */
42	  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;
43	  /** Fix D — PLP only (`VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.hideBagOnMobile` in index.tsx). A viewport-width
44	   *  concern, not a pointer-type one: hidden below `breakpoints.md`, visible from it up — see
45	   *  docblock point 5. */
46	  hideBagOnMobile?: boolean;
47	};
48	
49	/**
50	 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
51	 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
52	 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
53	 * own by itself:
54	 *
55	 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
56	 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
57	 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
58	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
59	 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
60	 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
61	 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
62	 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
63	 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
64	 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
65	 *      Three separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
66	 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
67	 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
68	 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but three plain keys need no such
69	 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
70	 *      ONE of the three (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
71	 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
72	 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close` and `carousel` are the two exceptions:
73	 *      `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly (`close` via
74	 *      `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute, top: 50%, ...`),
75	 *      so each needs (and gets) only the z-index bump here:
76	 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
77	 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
78	 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
79	 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
80	 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
81	 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
82	 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
83	 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
84	 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
85	 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
86	 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
87	 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
88	 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
89	 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
90	 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
91	 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
92	 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
93	 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
94	 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
95	 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
96	 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
97	 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
98	 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
99	 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
100	 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
101	 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
102	 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
103	 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
104	 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
105	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
106	 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:focus-within` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below) — `:hover`
107	 *      alone would leave every reveal permanently unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable
108	 *      device, since `display: none` removes the unconditional-state element from the tab order
109	 *      entirely and nothing but a real pointer hover could ever have revealed it.
110	 *   4. NOTIFY-ME'S HOVER GATE (Fix C, found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit against the
111	 *      real Figma Default+Hover Unavailable instances for all three variations, desktop AND
112	 *      mobile). Three behaviours confirmed together, all different from point 3 above:
113	 *        - `isUnavailable` suppresses the PLP/Wishlist size-selector swap entirely (index.tsx
114	 *          AND-s `hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` with `!isUnavailable` before they
115	 *          ever reach this recipe) — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price
116	 *          stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own `hoverRevealsPrice` is
117	 *          untouched by this — its Unavailable Hover reference still reveals price normally.
118	 *        - Suppressing that swap is not, by itself, enough to reproduce the reference: with no
119	 *          hide/reveal pair of its own, the size-chip wrapper falls back to Content's natural
120	 *          (visible) default and would show permanently — briefly shipped exactly that way mid-fix
121	 *          and caught by re-checking the real render against Figma, which shows size chips hidden
122	 *          in BOTH states when unavailable, not merely "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
123	 *          (index.tsx: `config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && isUnavailable`) carries that permanent
124	 *          hide as its own unconditional rule below — deliberately outside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`
125	 *          entirely, since unlike everything else here this isn't a pointer-type distinction at
126	 *          all: every device sees it hidden, full stop.
127	 *        - Notify-me itself is hover-gated the OPPOSITE way round from price/the size-selector:
128	 *          hidden by default and revealed on hover **only inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`**, not
129	 *          unconditionally. Every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it appearing only on
130	 *          hover; every Mobile Unavailable reference (Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so
131	 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no
132	 *          reveal needed. Putting the "hidden by default" half outside the media query — matching
133	 *          point 3's own structure literally — would have made notify-me permanently invisible on
134	 *          touch, since a touch pointer never matches `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` and so could never
135	 *          trigger the `:hover`/`:focus-within` half either.
136	 *   5. THE BAG ICON'S PLP-ONLY MOBILE HIDE (Fix D, same SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit). A genuinely
137	 *      different axis from points 3-4 above: `DESKTOP_QUERY` is a **viewport-width** media query
138	 *      (`min-width`), not `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`'s pointer-capability one — a large touch tablet and
139	 *      a small hover-capable laptop window need to agree with Figma's own Desktop/Mobile split by
140	 *      width, not by input method. Figma's PLP/PDP Mobile Card-content instance
141	 *      (`40002163:41479`) has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop's own PLP
142	 *      instance and Wishlist's Mobile instance (`40002187:58472`) both leave it visible — so this

145	 *      `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable`, Fix G's narrower Wishlist-only-when-out-of-stock rule —
146	 *      see index.tsx's own docblock and `bagHiddenOnMobile` derivation), not a blanket rule. This
147	 *      recipe only ever sees the one already-combined boolean — it has no opinion on which of the
148	 *      two reasons produced it. Hidden unconditionally by default (mobile-first, matching
149	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own padding step direction), then shown again from
150	 *      `DESKTOP_QUERY` up as `display: 'flex'` — not `'block'` — since that is the actual display
151	 *      type `bagWrapper`'s own recipe uses for its icon-centring; this selector's specificity
152	 *      (a class + two attribute selectors) beats Content's single class either way, so restoring
153	 *      the wrong display value would have silently flattened that centring rather than merely
154	 *      failing to apply — the inverse of point 3's hover-reveal shape, but the same "start from
155	 *      the narrowest/most restrictive case, widen from there" idea.
156	 *
157	 * Parts: only `root` is declared. Everything above is a nested descendant selector inside

159	 * a separate Chakra part — `index.tsx` never reads anything off `useMultiStyleConfig` but
160	 * `styles.root`, so `recipeParts.test.ts`'s declared-vs-read reconciliation needs nothing more.

/**
 * Shared DOM-contract constants for the ZimmProductCard organism and its composed molecules
 * (ZimmProductCardMedia, ZimmProductCardContent) — defined once here so every producer (the JSX
 * that stamps a `data-card-slot` attribute) and consumer (the organism's own recipe selectors,
 * plus this component family's test suites) reads the same value instead of each independently
 * retyping it. Same pattern, smaller scale, as `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`.
 */

/**
 * The ten `data-card-slot` attribute values that wire the organism's hover/reveal CSS
 * (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) to specific descendant DOM nodes. `media` / `badge` / `close` /
 * `carousel` / `indicator` are stamped by `ZimmProductCardMedia`; `content` / `bag` / `price` /
 * `sizeChips` / `notifyMe` by `ZimmProductCardContent`. Do not rename a value here without
 * checking both molecules' own docblocks, which document what each slot is for.
 */
export const CARD_SLOT = {
  media: 'media',
  badge: 'badge',
  close: 'close',
  carousel: 'carousel',
  indicator: 'indicator',
  content: 'content',
  bag: 'bag',
  price: 'price',
  sizeChips: 'sizeChips',
  notifyMe: 'notifyMe',
} as const;

/**
 * Hover-capable-pointer gate shared by every hover-only affordance across the card family
 * (desktop arrows, the hover-reveal price/size-selector swap, the notify-me reveal) — the
 * resolved SFCC-236 decision that arrows and the touch slide-indicator are mutually exclusive by
 * pointer capability, not viewport width.
 */
export const HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)';

I have not touched, reverted, or attempted to merge/resolve any of that — per my scope rules I only touch what my step names, and reverting someone else's in-flight work without being asked would be its own violation. Branch confirmed: `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (not `develop`/`main`).

### 1. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`

  display: 'flex',
},
[`&:focus-within [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {

with an inline comment matching the file's own convention, plus a new numbered docblock point (**point 6**) added after point 5, documenting the same rationale/evidence and cross-referencing the removal in the Media file.
